messages:
sam_s (Sales): Heads-up — Prospect (FinRegCo) sent a SIG/CAIQ and is asking several KMS/BYOK/HSM questions. They want explicit answers for at-rest, in-transit, and how we handle key rotation and split custody. Can we draft short bullets for the questionnaire?

ben_se (SE): I can take the tech bullets. Quick summary: at-rest: AES-256 envelope encryption + keys in KMS; in-transit: TLS1.3 with modern ciphers; customer-managed keys supported via AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault; HSM options via BYOK for Dedicated/Private.

lisa_sec (Security): Add note about FIPS/HSM compliance: we support FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs when customer brings keys or uses cloud HSM. For hosted, we offer integration with customer KMS (encrypted key material never persisted in plaintext on our side). Also call out audit logs and CMKs not exported.

maria_ae (AE): Prospect also asked: can we do key rotation monthly and retain ability to decrypt historical content? They need both rotation and data access guarantees.

ben_se (SE): Short answer: rotation is supported via key versioning and envelope rewrapping. We support rolling rewraps for new tokens; older ciphertext remains decryptable by previous key versions unless customer requests re-encryption of stored blobs. If they require periodical re-encryption, that’s an operational task we can run (POC scope).

joe_infra (Infra): For Dedicated/Private, customer can host a KMS/HSM in their VPC or on-prem and we support direct key lookup via internal connector (mutual TLS). For Hosted, we use an outbound encrypted connector to their cloud KMS; no plaintext keys stored.

sam_s (Sales): Can someone put that into 5 concise SIG answers I can paste? Also they asked for example config and a short assurance statement for vendor risk about key custody.

ben_se (SE): Draft SIG-style answers (short):
1) Encryption at-rest: All customer data persisted by Redwood is encrypted with AES-256. We use envelope encryption where data keys are encrypted by a customer- or Redwood-managed master key in a cloud KMS or HSM. (See: https://docs.redwood.com/security/encryption)
2) Encryption in-transit: All client<->service traffic is protected by TLS 1.3 with certificate pinning for service endpoints and strong cipher suites. Internal service-to-service traffic is mTLS.
3) Customer-managed keys / BYOK: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers may keep keys fully within their VPC or on-prem HSM. In Hosted mode we provide a connector pattern that does not persist key material in plaintext.
4) Key rotation and access: Key rotation is supported via KMS key versioning. Previous key versions remain available for decryption; we can run rewrapping workflows to re-encrypt stored data under new keys on request. Rotation cadence is configurable; we recommend policies aligned to customer/regulatory requirements (e.g., 90 days for high-sensitivity data).
5) Audit & controls: All KMS key usage is logged. We provide audit trails for key creation, usage, rotation, and deletion. Access is governed by least privilege IAM, role separation, and optional HSM-based split custody when required.

lisa_sec (Security): Add this assurance snippet for vendor risk review: "Redwood Inference does not export customer master keys. When integrated with customer-managed KMS/HSM, master keys remain under customer control. For hosted integrations, Redwood holds only encrypted data keys; unencrypted key material is never written to persistent storage. All key operations are logged and available for audit."

maria_ae (AE): Prospect also asked for technical proof-of-concept (POC) steps to validate BYOK. Suggested minimal plan: 1) enable connector to their KMS in staging, 2) perform sign/encrypt/decrypt test vectors, 3) run a rotate cycle, 4) validate logs and audit exports. Estimate: 3-5 days + security review.

ben_se (SE): Example connector snippet to include in POC doc (curl style):
```
curl -X POST https://connector.redwood.local/v1/register \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -d '{"kms_provider":"aws","key_arn":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"}'
```
Note: in Hosted we use short-lived certs for the connector and mutual TLS.

sam_s (Sales): Perfect. One more: they asked whether we support HSM import vs. wrapping keys with cloud KMS. Quick phrasing?

lisa_sec (Security): We support both patterns: import of key material into an HSM (where policy allows) and envelope keys wrapped by a cloud HSM-backed KMS. We recommend wrapping keys in a cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM or KMS with HSM-backed CMKs) for easier lifecycle management unless the customer requires on-prem import for regulatory reasons.

joe_infra (Infra): Operational notes: if they require split custody we can coordinate an HSM vendor plug (Thales/Entrust) and set up an HSM-backed key program. That adds coordination and time (vendor procurement + network setup).

sec-bot: Automated note: See internal playbook: https://confluence.redwood.local/display/SRV/KMS+Integration+Playbook for steps and required artifacts for an enterprise BYOK review.

maria_ae (AE): I'll send the five SIG answers + assurance snippet and POC outline to FinRegCo this afternoon. Team — if someone can DM me the connector sample with redacted ARNs, I’ll attach. :thumbsup:

ben_se (SE): I'll DM the snippet and can join the kickoff call next week.

sam_s (Sales): Thanks everyone — this helps a lot. If POC shows any blockers we'll loop in security for a deeper review.
